citation.title: A Student's t filter for heavy tailed process and measurement noise
citation.authors: Michael Roth; Emre Özkan; Fredrik Gustafsson
citation.venue: Proceedings of the 38th IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
citation.doi_or_arxiv: 10.1109/ICASSP.2013.6638770 (from the supplied identifier hint; the extracted text does not show the DOI, so check it)

topic: Recursive filtering in linear state-space models with Student's t (heavy-tailed) process and measurement noise.
own_question: How can Kalman-type filtering be made robust to outliers in both process and measurement noise while keeping a simple, low-cost recursion?
actual_method_and_evidence: The paper derives an exact t filter. In it the degrees-of-freedom parameter grows at each update, so the filter converges to a Kalman filter. It then proposes approximations that keep the tails heavy, using a minimum-dof choice and matrix rescaling that preserves probability regions. The posterior scale depends on the innovation. Evidence is one simulated constant-velocity tracking scenario with outliers drawn from a Gaussian mixture. Results are reported for one realization and for Monte Carlo runs. There is no plasma, CES or real-data evaluation.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Student's t state-space filters provide a Kalman-like recursion in which the update scale depends on the innovation. This offers one conceptual option for outlier-robust causal updating.
claim_checks.qualification: This is background theory only. It was not implemented in our study unless we actually implement it, and the paper's evidence is simulation only.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not applicable. This is generic simulated tracking with no diagnostic timing.
validation_if_relevant: Simulation only: 500 steps per run and 1000 Monte Carlo runs. There is no untouched real data.
forbidden_inferences: That it validates any estimator on CES, BES or ECEI data
That heavy-tailed filtering improves our nowcasts
That its simulated error gains transfer to fusion diagnostics
That it addresses 10 ms computation in our setting
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Cite it optionally in the theoretical background, and only if we discuss robust recursive or Kalman-type baselines. It does not bear on the core framing.
